next_step_summary: The post-PR #273 rerun of the reviewed March-August 2025 contract eventually succeeded on gemini-3.6-flash in cycle 4 after nine retryable failures. PR #272 materially improved the report: AS-IS was narrowed by repair protections; the 21-day return inspection / 10-day correction process survived alongside holdover; invented market/numeric rewrite advice disappeared; generic missing clauses and proposed changes were suppressed. Two core semantic gaps remained: the 20,000 NIS security-cheque mechanism surfaced only a subset of the required realization questions, and broad fundamental-breach wording was still not fully reconciled with the contract's specific 7-day rent cure/notice mechanics. Product-owner correction: the model may no longer treat the deterministic inventory as an internal checklist. PR #274 adds an explicit `question_engine_answers` extraction layer with exactly one answer per core question_id, positional values matching every declared answer_field, controlled answer states, and evidence-block references. Python rejects missing, duplicate, unknown, structurally incomplete, inconsistent, or source-invalid Question Engine answers before accepting the provider result; the existing cyclic route can then try the next model. No OCR, privacy boundary, provider/model list, dependency, permission, workflow, storage, or endpoint change. After PR #274 merge, rerun the same contract and inspect the explicit answers for `security.realization_chain`, `security.return_mechanics`, `security.completion_authority`, `termination.notice_cure`, and `termination.cross_clause_interaction` before broadening to other contracts.
